newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-DWYER CALLS FOR RADICAL CHANGES.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-DWYER CALLS FOR RADICAL CHANGES.

text.p: On the eve of the annual meeting of the Rugby Football Union, former Australian coach Bob Dwyer has called for radical changes in the game's administration both in England and abroad.

"Rugby administrations around the world, from my observation, don't have any accountability," said Dwyer, director of coaching at Leicester since July last year. "Change the structure concerning their appointments."
Dwyer, now 56, coached the Wallabies to their World Cup triumph at Twickenham in 1991 and is still hungry for success.
"I'm not oblivious to the fact that if you're not successful you might lose your job," he said. "It doesn't drive me to do my job though.
"Something else drives me much more than that, which is just what I want to be successful."
Dwyer is highly critical of several aspects of the English game.

"Easily the biggest problem with the game in England is that they don't have competitive leagues for youth teams or development teams or even second teams," he said. "Im astonished that it's taken so long."
He is also pushing for a greater share of gate takings, saying: "The most successful clubs have got to earn the most money."
Bad weather has also been a challenge for Dwyer, as has the English reluctance to overcome the playing hazards it poses.
The Australian had anticipated frozen grounds but not the lack of alternative venues for training.
"It's been cold here for a long time," he said.
Drought-ridden grounds were also an unpleasant surprise as was the lack of watering systems.
Dwyer overcame these and other obstacles to take Leicester to success in the Pilkington Cup and a place in the European Cup.
"He's a very respected Australian," said England Director of Rugby Don Rutherford. "People will sit up and listen."
Dwyer still has goals in the game.

"When people are talking in years and years to come about the greatest teams of all time, they'll say: 'What about the Wallabies of 1991 or what about the Leicester team of 1998? They're a contender.' That's what I want them to say. I don't want to do anything ordinary."
